pages.text: Mr. Horse's cart rattled up the hill road. They were visiting Grandma's farm. "Still far, Mr. Horse?" Pipo gripped his scarf. "Just over the hill," quick-stepping Mr. Horse answered.
A stone-wall farm appeared beyond the hill. Grandma's farm. Pipo stayed in the cart, hiding behind a hay sack. "I cannot remember Grandma's face... I want to go home."
Grandma came from the door with a cloth bundle. "Oh, our Pipo is here!" He lay flatter on the cart floor. "Hello..." His voice disappeared into the hay sack.
Beside the cart, Grandma opened the bundle. Fresh bread steamed. "Try a piece while it is warm." Pipo took one and ate. Sweet.
Pipo hopped down. Grandma held his hand and went to the pen. "Want to hold this lamb?" He held it in both hands. Soft and snug. "Wow, warm!"
Mr. Horse whispered, "Knowing you were coming, Grandma has baked bread and made a hay bed for days." In the shed stood a bed just Pipo's size. His heart felt touched.
Pipo ran and nestled onto Grandma's lap. "Grandma, hug me!" It was the softest, warmest lap in the world. "Snuggle onto Grandma's lap!" He rubbed his face against her and smiled.
Outside, the pen gate creaked shut. Nearly bedtime. Grandma told old stories by the stove. Pipo listened, crouching before her with hands at his chest.

After a sound sleep in the hay bed, morning came. Sheep left the pen, saying baa. Pipo counted on his fingers. "One, say hello! Two, try what she offers! Three, snuggle on her lap!" Mr. Horse brought the cart to the gate. Tears rose. "Grandma, I will come again!"
Grandma sat Pipo on her lap and hugged him. Beside her, the bread bundle lay open. "Even someone unfamiliar feels close after a snug hug." "Snuggle onto Grandma's lap!" Pipo kissed her cheek.
